gaps.fact: The span from 17 to 53 degrees south and the greatest width of about 350 km are never taught; the chapter gives only rarely two hundred kilometres wide, which is the typical width, not the Court's figure.
The Coastal Range as a rain shadow against the cold Pacific: the Codex treats the range only as a wall against fog and sea air, never as the reason the Central Valley is drier.

The Court gives sand as Chile's soil and says phylloxera is absent because of sandy soil; every Chilean chapter, question and article explains the absence by geographic isolation alone (i-br3wyy4p offers no sand option), and sand is linked to Chile only in the general chapters vit and Viticulture & Winemaking. A candidate meeting the Court's wording should recognise both reasons.

The DO is an origin statement only, with no other rules, and its four tiers run Region, Subregion, Zone, Area: only the country ladder says so; no question names the tiers or asks what a Chilean DO governs.
The Valle Central makes about 80 per cent of Chilean wine, and the Maipo surrounds Santiago and holds most of the major historical wineries: neither figure nor fact is asked or stated in a chapter.
Chilean wine is often big, intense, fruit driven and high in alcohol: no chapter or question gives the general style, and the Codex's emphasis on the cool coast leaves the Court's picture untaught.

Santa Rita, Errázuriz, Casa Lapostolle and Carmen are never the key to a Régionale or Village question (Santa Rita and Errázuriz stand only as wrong options in i-b72qf5n1, Santa Rita indirectly in c-erl8k66o). Lapostolle is keyed only by the colchagua article question r-52b5t6l6, and Carmen appears only in the Chilean articles (maipo-valley, the country overview and traps) and their region cards, never in a question.

The 1600s Spanish laws restricting colonial wine production, and the 1800s independence with the European immigrants and French cuttings (Ochagavía, 1851) that expanded viticulture: the restriction appears nowhere in the Codex, and the nineteenth century only in the country overview.

courtUpdates.now: The four tiers stand, but Decreto 464 was amended by a decree published in the Diario Oficial on 14 May 2025: the Austral region is redrawn from the province of Cautín southward, and two island denominations are added, Chiloé and Rapa Nui (Isla de Pascua), after a July 2024 announcement that also admitted 39 new grape varieties. The country article carries the 2025 decree and Chiloé but not Rapa Nui.
courtUpdates.source: Search: Diario Oficial de la República de Chile, 14 May 2025 (Decreto 27 of 2024, modifying Decreto 464); SAG and ODEPA announcements of 30 July 2024 on new varieties and denominations; a second search confirmed Rapa Nui beside Chiloé.

notes: Mapped questions: South America holds Régionale 60 and Village 23, 83 in all, shared with Argentina; by country, Chile has Régionale 29 and Village 8 (37), Argentina Régionale 26 and Village 9 (35), Uruguay and Brazil Régionale 5 and Village 6 (11). Outside the mapped cats, i-b72qf5n1 and c-lc9eawhv (Producers & Icons), i-qb7gj70n, i-0x24pbu4, i-kbvqvdcf and i-i21dlop9 (Geography & Maps) and c-erl8k66o (California) also touch Chile. The Régionale chapter and bank are strong on the map: the Central Valley's four in order, Rapel with Cachapoal and Colchagua, Casablanca and Leyda, Limarí, Apalta, Peumo, Puente Alto, Itata and Maule, the Humboldt Current and camanchaca, Costa, Entre Cordilleras and Andes, the 75 and 85 per cent rules, phylloxera's absence and the Carménère story with its 1994 date. The Village bank, at eight Chilean stems, never asks the Certified producer list, and the History row's colonial and nineteenth century dates are untaught. No factual error found: Carménère 1994 and its 1998 registration, Torres at Curicó in 1979, Don Melchor of 1987, the 2011 position terms, the 2018 areas, the Reserva alcohol lines and the Decreto 464 regions all hold. The Court's 2,670 miles with 4300 km, and its 217 miles with 350 km, are its own figures (the width is the maximum). House rule notes for the owner: i-oxyer4y6 names a living ampelographer in its explanation, and i-hpotlk9o names Miguel Torres, a living person as well as the firm's name. Two searches spent: Decreto 464 since 2023, and a second in this pass confirming that the 2025 amendment (Decreto 27 of 2024, published 14 May 2025) admits both Chiloé and Rapa Nui. Reviewed again in this pass: every cited id exists in its stated category, the country split of the 83 South America stems was recounted, and the article questions (r- ids) were read for the producer row.
